location.story: The King’s Son and the Painted Lion

approved_translation: We had better bear our troubles bravely than try to escape them.
context_summary: A KING, whose only son was fond of martial exercises, had a dream in which he was warned that his son would be killed by a lion. Afraid the dream should prove true, he built for his son a pleasant palace and adorned its walls for his amusement with all kinds of life-sized animals, among which was the picture of a lion. But one of the tree’s prickles pierced his finger and caused great pain and inflammation, so that the young Prince fell down in a fainting fit. A violent fever suddenly set in, from which he died not many days later. We had better bear our troubles bravely than try to escape them.
interpretation_boundaries: Keep animals as naturalistic, not anthropomorphic
Focus on the moral lesson, not on violent or graphic details
